# Documento: en/ScriptReference/Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.html

# PhysicsWorld

struct in
Unity.U2D.Physics

Leave feedback

Suggest a change

## Success!

Thank you for helping us improve the quality of Unity Documentation. Although we cannot accept all submissions, we do read each suggested change from our users and will make updates where applicable.

Close

## Submission failed

For some reason your suggested change could not be submitted. Please <a>try again</a> in a few minutes. And thank you for taking the time to help us improve the quality of Unity Documentation.

Close

Your name

Your email

Suggestion\*


Submit suggestion

Cancel

### Description

A world is a container for all other physics objects such as [PhysicsBody](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.html"), [PhysicsShape](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.html"), [PhysicsJoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.html") etc.
A world can be simulated in isolation from all other worlds.
The maximum number of worlds that can be created at one time is defined by [PhysicsCoreSettings2D.maximumWorlds](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D-maximumWorlds.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D-maximumWorlds.html").
A world is completely isolated from all other worlds.

### Static Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [aabbMargin](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-aabbMargin.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-aabbMargin.html") | Get the distance used to expand AABBs in the broadphase dynamic tree, in meters. This allows broadphase proxies to move by a small amount without triggering a tree adjustment. This value is 0.05f \* PhysicsWorld.lengthUnitsPerMeter. Normally this is 5cm. |
| [alwaysDrawWorlds](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-alwaysDrawWorlds.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-alwaysDrawWorlds.html") | Get if worlds are always drawn independent of whether rendering is currently active or not as specified by PhysicsWorld.renderingMode. When true, world drawing is always active and a PhysicsEvents.WorldDrawResults event is produced containing the DrawResults. When false, world drawing only occurs depending on the PhysicsWorld.renderingMode setting. This can be controlled via PhysicsCoreSettings2D.alwaysDrawWorlds. |
| [bodyMaxRotation](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bodyMaxRotation.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bodyMaxRotation.html") | Get the maximum rotation of a body per time step, in degrees. This limit is very large and is used to prevent numerical problems. This value is approximately 45-degrees or 0.25f \* PhysicsMath.PI radians. |
| [bodyTimeToSleep](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bodyTimeToSleep.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bodyTimeToSleep.html") | Get the time that a body must be still before it will go to sleep, in seconds. This value is 0.5 seconds. |
| [concurrentSimulations](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-concurrentSimulations.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-concurrentSimulations.html") | Gets how many simulations can be started in parallel. Whilst running simulations in parallel can improver overall performance, workers should ideally be left free for the simulation solver otherwise it may degrade solving performance. The actual quantity of workers used will always be capped to those available on the current device. If the total number of workers available is below 4 then parallel simulation won't occur as generally this would reduce overall performance, however parallel solving of each simulation using workers will still be used. This should not be confused with the quantity of workers used when solving a simulation. |
| [contactFilterGroupMode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFilterGroupMode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFilterGroupMode.html") | Get the current value of PhysicsCoreSettings2D.contactFilterGroupMode. |
| [contactFilterMode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFilterMode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFilterMode.html") | Get the current value of PhysicsCoreSettings2D.contactFilterMode. |
| [defaultWorld](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-defaultWorld.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-defaultWorld.html") | Get the default world created at start-up. This world cannot be destroyed as it is permanently owned by Unity itself. See PhysicsWorld.SetOwner and PhysicsWorld.isOwned. |
| [disableSimulation](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-disableSimulation.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-disableSimulation.html") | Get if the automatic simulation of any PhysicsWorld is temporarily disabled. When true, no automatic simulation will occur. When false, normal operation occurs with automatic simulation. This can be controlled via PhysicsCoreSettings2D.disableSimulation. |
| [globalCounters](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-globalCounters.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-globalCounters.html") | Get the world counters, summed for all the active worlds. |
| [globalProfile](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-globalProfile.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-globalProfile.html") | Get the world timing profile, summed for all the active worlds. |
| [hugeWorldExtent](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-hugeWorldExtent.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-hugeWorldExtent.html") | Gets what physics considers a large extent in the world. Positions greater than approximately 16km will have precision problems, so 100km as a limit should be fine in all cases. This is used to detect bad values. This value is 100000.0f \* PhysicsWorld.lengthUnitsPerMeter. |
| [isRenderingAllowed](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isRenderingAllowed.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isRenderingAllowed.html") | Get if rendering is currently allowed. Rendering is always allowed in the Editor however it is only allowed elsewhere depending on PhysicsCoreSettings2D.renderingMode. |
| [lengthUnitsPerMeter](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-lengthUnitsPerMeter.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-lengthUnitsPerMeter.html") | Get the internal length units per meter. Changes won't take effect until exiting play mode. The physics system relates all length units on meters but you may need different units for your project. You can set this value to use different units but it should only be modified before any other calls to the physics system occur and only modified once. Changing this value after any physics object has been created can result in severe simulation instabilities. For example, if your game uses pixels for units you can use pixels for all length values sent to the physics system. There should be no extra cost however, the physics system has some internal tolerances and thresholds that have been tuned for meters. By calling this function, the physics system is better able to adjust those tolerances and thresholds to improve accuracy. A good rule of thumb is to pass the height of your player character to this function. So if your player character is 32 pixels high, then pass 32 to this function. Then you may confidently use pixels for all the length values sent to the physics system. All length values returned from the physics system will also then be in pixels because the physics system does not do any scaling internally, however, you are now on the hook for coming up with good values for gravity, density, and forces. The default value is 1. |
| [linearSlop](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-linearSlop.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-linearSlop.html") | Get the small length used as a collision and constraint tolerance, in meters. Usually it is chosen to be numerically significant, but visually insignificant. This value is 0.005f \* PhysicsWorld.lengthUnitsPerMeter. Normally this is 0.5cm. |
| [maximumWorldsAllocated](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-maximumWorldsAllocated.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-maximumWorldsAllocated.html") | Get the actual allocated maximum worlds available. This can differ at runtime from PhysicsCoreSettings2D.maximumWorlds if it was changed and the physics system has not been restarted. Another reason this can differ would be if there was not available memory to allocate the requested maximum worlds. |
| [renderingMode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-renderingMode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-renderingMode.html") | Get the current value of PhysicsCoreSettings2D.renderingMode. NOTE: Drawing and rendering are always available in the Unity Editor however rendering requires compute buffer support on any device it is used without which no rendering will occur. |
| [safetyLocksEnabled](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-safetyLocksEnabled.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-safetyLocksEnabled.html") | Get/Set whether safety threading locks are enabled or not. Locks are enabled by default however on platforms that do not support threading, locks are not used. Disabling locks can result in a small performance boost however, please note the following EXTREME CAUTIONS. Typically, per-world, multiple read operations can happen in parallel however only a single write operation can occur concurrently. Read and write operations can never happen at the same time. Locking is a self-balancing reader-preferred system that tries to reduce writers "starving". Once a writer is in a queue, it registers incoming readers as waiting readers and, once active readers are handled, it starts processing a single writer. After that writer has been handled, it flips waiting readers into active readers and processes them. Whilst this system is extremely fast, it does have a very small overhead. Disabling this system can give a small performance boost but is nearly always not worth it therefore this option should be used for testing only. EXTREME CAUTION should be taken if disabling locks on platforms that support threading! A majority of this API is thread-safe and is is due to the safety locks! Locks are used to ensure that read and write operations do not interfere with each other. Locks also ensure that no read or write operations happen during a simulation step. Overlapping read or write operations will almost certainly result in corruptions and a subsequent crash, so unless you are absolutely sure this is not the case, do not disable locks! |
| [speculativeContactDistance](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-speculativeContactDistance.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-speculativeContactDistance.html") | Get the distance at which speculative contacts will be calculated. This reduces jitter. This value is 4.0f \* PhysicsWorld.lengthUnitsPerMeter. Normally this is 2cm. |
| [transformChangeMode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformChangeMode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformChangeMode.html") | Get the current value of PhysicsCoreSettings2D.transformChangeMode. See TransformChangeMode. |
| [usePhysicsLayers](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-usePhysicsLayers.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-usePhysicsLayers.html") | Get if the option of PhysicsCoreSettings2D.usePhysicsLayers is active or not. If no PhysicsCoreSettings2D asset is assigned, this option will return false (inactive). When active, the physics 64-bit layers are used (see PhysicsCoreSettings2D.physicsLayerNames) for property drawers and PhysicsLayers.GetLayerMask. When inactive, the 32-bit layers are used (see LayerMask) for property drawers and PhysicsLayers.GetLayerMask. In all cases, the physics system itself will always use the full 64-bit layers assigned, however when using 32-bit layers, the top 32-bits will be set to zero. |
| [worldCount](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-worldCount.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-worldCount.html") | Get the number of created worlds. This will be a value in the range of 1 to PhysicsCoreSettings2D.maximumWorlds. |

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [autoBodyUpdateCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoBodyUpdateCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoBodyUpdateCallbacks.html") | Controls if body update callback targets are automatically called. See PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacks |
| [autoContactCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoContactCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoContactCallbacks.html") | Controls if shape contact callback targets are automatically called. See PhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacks |
| [autoJointThresholdCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoJointThresholdCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoJointThresholdCallbacks.html") | Controls if joint threshold callback targets are automatically called. See PhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks |
| [autoTriggerCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoTriggerCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-autoTriggerCallbacks.html") | Controls if shape trigger callback targets are automatically called. See PhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacks |
| [awakeBodyCount](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-awakeBodyCount.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-awakeBodyCount.html") | Get the number of awake bodies in the world. |
| [bodyUpdateEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bodyUpdateEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bodyUpdateEvents.html") | Get the body events from the last simulation. The PhysicsBody objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsBody.isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See BodyUpdateEvent. |
| [bounceThreshold](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bounceThreshold.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-bounceThreshold.html") | Adjust the bounce threshold, usually in meters per second. It is recommended not to make this value very small because it will prevent bodies from sleeping. |
| [capacity](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-capacity.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-capacity.html") | Get the current world capacities reached since the world was created. This reflects the peak object counts and can be used to presize a PhysicsWorldDefinition.capacity for similar worlds. See PhysicsWorldDefinition.capacity. |
| [contactBeginEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactBeginEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactBeginEvents.html") | Get the contact begin events from the last simulation. The PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsShape.isValid). The Contact objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced. Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See ContactBeginEvent. |
| [contactDamping](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactDamping.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactDamping.html") | The contact bounciness with 1 being critical damping (non-dimensional). |
| [contactEndEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactEndEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactEndEvents.html") | Get the contact end events from the last simulation. The PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsShape.isValid). The Contact objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced. Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See ContactEndEvent. |
| [contactFilterCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFilterCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFilterCallbacks.html") | Controls if contact filter callbacks will be called. A contact filter callback allows direct control over whether a contact will be created between a pair of shapes. This applies to both triggers and non-triggers but only with Dynamic bodies. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A contact filter callback will call the PhysicsShape.callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement IContactFilterCallback. |
| [contactFrequency](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFrequency.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactFrequency.html") | The contact stiffness, in cycles per second. |
| [contactHitEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactHitEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactHitEvents.html") | Get the contact hit events from the last simulation. The PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsShape.isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See ContactHitEvent. |
| [contactHitEventThreshold](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactHitEventThreshold.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactHitEventThreshold.html") | The contact hit event threshold controls the collision speed needed to generate a contact hit event, usually in meters per second. See ContactHitEvent. |
| [contactRecycleDistance](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactRecycleDistance.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactRecycleDistance.html") | The contact recycle distance, in meters. Setting this to zero disables contact point recycling. Contact recycling reuses contact points across simulation time-steps when the relative movement is small. This feature improves stability and performance by around 25% (approximately). Contact points are not recalculated until shapes move more than 5cm (default) relative to each other. Contact recycling skips some updates such as friction, pre-solve (etc) until the contacts are no longer recycled. |
| [contactSpeed](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactSpeed.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactSpeed.html") | The contact speed used to solve overlaps, in meters per second. |
| [continuousAllowed](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-continuousAllowed.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-continuousAllowed.html") | Controls if continuous collision detection will be used between Dynamic and Static bodies. Generally you should keep continuous collision enabled to prevent fast moving objects from going through Static objects. The performance gain from disabling continuous collision is minor. |
| [counters](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-counters.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-counters.html") | Get the world counters. |
| [definition](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-definition.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-definition.html") | Get/Set a world definition by accessing all of its current properties. This is provided as convenience only and should not be used when performance is important as all the properties defined in the definition are accessed sequentially. You should try to only use the specific properties you need rather than using this feature. |
| [drawColors](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawColors.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawColors.html") | Controls what colors are used to draw PhysicsBody, PhysicsShape, PhysicsJoint etc. |
| [drawContactType](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawContactType.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawContactType.html") | Controls the DrawContactType used when drawing contact points. |
| [drawFillAlpha](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawFillAlpha.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawFillAlpha.html") | Controls the draw fill alpha. This is used to scale the interior fill alpha and is only used when PhysicsWorld.DrawFillOptions.Outline is used so that the interior color can be distinguished from the outline color by transparency. |
| [drawFillOptions](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawFillOptions.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawFillOptions.html") | Controls how shape geometry is filled when drawing. See DrawFillOptions. |
| [drawFilter](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawFilter.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawFilter.html") | Limits what gets drawn to a narrow selection. This only affects DrawOptions that are drawing all bodies, shapes etc. It does not affect selected elements or custom drawing. See IgnoreFilter. |
| [drawForceScale](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawForceScale.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawForceScale.html") | Controls the joint contact force scale used when drawing contact forces. |
| [drawNormalScale](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawNormalScale.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawNormalScale.html") | Controls the joint contact normal scale used when drawing contact normals. |
| [drawOptions](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawOptions.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawOptions.html") | Limits what gets drawn to a broad selection. See DrawOptions. |
| [drawPointScale](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawPointScale.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawPointScale.html") | Controls the draw point scale used when drawing points. |
| [drawThickness](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawThickness.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-drawThickness.html") | Controls the draw thickness (outline and orientation). |
| [elementDepth](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-elementDepth.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-elementDepth.html") | Controls the element depth. When using custom drawing of geometry or primitive shapes there is no reference to the orthogonal axis used with respect to the current PhysicsWorld.transformPlane. The element depth is in world-space and for each transform plan is defined as: Element depth is rendered along the Z axis when using PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.XY.Element depth is rendered along the Y axis when using PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.XZ.Element depth is rendered along the X axis when using PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.ZY. You should set the element depth before performing any custom draw. The element depth will be reset to zero when rendering is complete. |
| [generation](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-generation.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-generation.html") | Get the world handle generation. |
| [gravity](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-gravity.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-gravity.html") | Get/Set the gravity vector applied to all bodies in the world, usually in m/s^2. |
| [index](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-index.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-index.html") | Get the world handle index. |
| [isDefaultWorld](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isDefaultWorld.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isDefaultWorld.html") | Check if this is the default PhysicsWorld. The default world is automatically created at start-up. |
| [isEmpty](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isEmpty.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isEmpty.html") | Check if the world is empty as defined by having no bodies, shapes or joints. |
| [isOwned](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isOwned.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isOwned.html") | Get if the world is owned. See PhysicsWorld.SetOwner. |
| [isValid](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isValid.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-isValid.html") | Check if the world is valid. |
| [jointThresholdEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-jointThresholdEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-jointThresholdEvents.html") | Get the joint events from the last simulation. An event is produced by a Joint which exceeds either its PhysicsJoint.forceThreshold or PhysicsJoint.torqueThreshold. The PhysicsJoint objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsJoint.isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See JointThresholdEvent. |
| [lastSimulationDeltaTime](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-lastSimulationDeltaTime.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-lastSimulationDeltaTime.html") | Get the delta-time used for the last simulation run. |
| [lastSimulationTimestamp](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-lastSimulationTimestamp.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-lastSimulationTimestamp.html") | Get the timestamp when the last simulation was run. |
| [maximumLinearSpeed](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-maximumLinearSpeed.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-maximumLinearSpeed.html") | Get/Set the maximum linear speed. |
| [ownerUserData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-ownerUserData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-ownerUserData.html") | Get PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only. |
| [paused](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-paused.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-paused.html") | Get/Set if the world is paused. When paused, any simulation attempted will be ignored whether it be automatic or manual. |
| [preSolveCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-preSolveCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-preSolveCallbacks.html") | Controls if pre-solve callbacks will be called. This only applies to Dynamic bodies and is ignored for triggers. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A pre-solve callback will call the PhysicsShape.callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement IPreSolveCallback. |
| [profile](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-profile.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-profile.html") | Get the world timing profile. |
| [simulationSubSteps](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-simulationSubSteps.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-simulationSubSteps.html") | Get/Set the simulation sub-steps to use during simulation. See PhysicsWorld.Simulate. |
| [simulationType](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-simulationType.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-simulationType.html") | Get/Set the simulation type which controls when or if the simulation will be automatically simulated. See SimulationType. |
| [simulationWorkers](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-simulationWorkers.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-simulationWorkers.html") | Get/Set the simulation worker count for the world. A single simulation worker is always used for simulation therefore a worker count of one means single thread simulation only. The actual quantity of workers used will always be capped to those available on the current device and reading the property will return the number of workers actually being used by the device. Changing the worker count continuously is not recommend and will impact performance as it requires the task queue be recreated. See PhysicsWorldDefinition.simulationWorkers. |
| [sleepingAllowed](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-sleepingAllowed.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-sleepingAllowed.html") | Controls if bodies go to sleep when not moving and not interacting. Sleeping can provide a significant performance improvement when many Dynamic or Kinematic bodies are in the world. |
| [syncInterpolation](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-syncInterpolation.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-syncInterpolation.html") | Controls if an extra write pass prior to the script fixed-update callback is made for any interpolation tweens to ensure that transforms are synchronized to the final body pose. Because this is an extra write pass, it has an impact on overall performance so only enable if you require transforms synchronized this way. NOTE: This only affects PhysicsBody that have their PhysicsBody.transformWriteMode set to PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Interpolate. |
| [transformPlane](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformPlane.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformPlane.html") | Controls the transform plane that the world uses when writing transforms. See PhysicsWorld.transformWriteMode. |
| [transformPlaneCustom](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformPlaneCustom.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformPlaneCustom.html") | Controls the transformation for the PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.Custom to allow transformation writing and reading to/from a custom 2D plane. See TransformPlaneCustom. |
| [transformTweenMode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformTweenMode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformTweenMode.html") | Controls if and how Transform tweens are calculated and/or written. Transform tweening is where bodies that have their PhysicsBody.transformObject set, write to the Transform each frame depending on the specific body TransformWriteMode set. Regardless of this setting, Transform tweening is never used if the PhysicsWorld.simulationType is PhysicsWorld.SimulationType.Update or PhysicsWorld.transformWriteMode is PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.Off. |
| [transformWriteCallbackTarget](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformWriteCallbackTarget.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformWriteCallbackTarget.html") | Get/Set the custom Object that implements the ITransformWriteCallback to which TransformWriteEvent and TransformTweenWriteEvent will be sent. The callback will only occur if PhysicsWorld.transformWriteMode is set to PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.Custom and there are PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents available. The object assigned here will be kept alive, not allowing the GC to dispose of it. To remove the object assigned here, set the callback target to NULL. |
| [transformWriteMode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformWriteMode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-transformWriteMode.html") | Controls how transform writing is handled. Only bodies that have their PhysicsBody.transformWriteMode active and produce a BodyUpdateEvent will write to a transform. See TransformWriteMode. |
| [triggerBeginEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-triggerBeginEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-triggerBeginEvents.html") | Get the trigger begin events from the last simulation. The PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsShape.isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See TriggerBeginEvent. |
| [triggerEndEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-triggerEndEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-triggerEndEvents.html") | Get the trigger end events from the last simulation. The PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see PhysicsShape.isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See TriggerEndEvent. |
| [userData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-userData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-userData.html") | Get/Set PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose. This cannot be set on the PhysicsWorld.defaultWorld and will always be at the default. The physics system doesn't use this data, it is entirely for custom use. |
| [warmStartingAllowed](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-warmStartingAllowed.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-warmStartingAllowed.html") | Is warm-starting allowed in the world? Disabling warming-starting will severely impact stability. This is typically used for testing only! |

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [CastGeometry](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastGeometry.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastGeometry.html") | Returns the shape(s) that intersect the specified Circle geometry as it is cast through the world. See QueryFilter, WorldCastMode, WorldCastResult and Collections.Allocator |
| [CastMover](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastMover.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastMover.html") | Cast a "Mover" which is geometry designed to collide with the world and solve its movement. Everything is specified via the WorldMoverInput with results returned in WorldMoverResult. |
| [CastRay](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastRay.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastRay.html") | Returns the shape(s) that intersect the specified Ray. Technically this is a line-segment and not an infinite ray. See QueryFilter, WorldCastMode, WorldCastResult and Collections.Allocator. |
| [CastShape](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastShape.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastShape.html") | Returns the shape(s) that intersect the specified shape as it is cast through the world. The selected shape is excluded from any results and must be in this world otherwise a warning will be produced. Neither PhysicsShape.ShapeType.Segment or PhysicsShape.ShapeType.ChainSegment shape types are supported. See QueryFilter, WorldCastMode, WorldCastResult and Collections.Allocator. |
| [CastShapeProxy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastShapeProxy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CastShapeProxy.html") | Returns the shape(s) that intersect the specified Circle geometry as it is cast through the world. See QueryFilter, WorldCastMode, WorldCastResult and Collections.Allocator. |
| [ClearDraw](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.ClearDraw.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.ClearDraw.html") | Clear all the custom drawn items. |

| [CreateBodyBatch](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateBodyBatch.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateBodyBatch.html") | Create a batch of bodies in the world. |
| [CreateJoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateJoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateJoint.html") | Create a PhysicsDistanceJoint in the world. See PhysicsDistanceJoint.Create. |
| [Destroy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Destroy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Destroy.html") | Destroy a world, destroying all objects contained within it such as all PhysicsBody and attached PhysicsShape and PhysicsJoint. If the object is owned with PhysicsWorld.SetOwner then you must provide the owner key it returned. Failing to do so will return a warning and the world will not be destroyed. You cannot destroy the PhysicsWorld.defaultWorld as it is permanently owned by Unity itself. |

| [DrawCircle](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawCircle.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawCircle.html") | Draw a Circle outline. For further information on the parameters, see CircleGeometry. |
| [DrawGeometry](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawGeometry.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawGeometry.html") | Draw the specified Circle Geometry. |
| [DrawLine](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawLine.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawLine.html") | Draw a Line. |
| [DrawLineStrip](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawLineStrip.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawLineStrip.html") | Draw a set of vertices as lines joined to each other. |
| [DrawPoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawPoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawPoint.html") | Draw a Point. A Point is similar to a filled Circle except the radius here is specified in pixels rather than world units. |
| [DrawQueryCastGeometry](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastGeometry.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastGeometry.html") | Draw the PhysicsWorld.CastGeometry query input. |
| [DrawQueryCastRay](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastRay.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastRay.html") | Draw the PhysicsWorld.CastRay query input. |
| [DrawQueryCastShape](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastShape.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastShape.html") | Draw the PhysicsWorld.CastShape query input. |
| [DrawQueryCastShapeProxy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastShapeProxy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryCastShapeProxy.html") | Draw the PhysicsWorld.CastShapeProxy query input. |
| [DrawQueryResult](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryResult.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawQueryResult.html") | Draw the CastResult returned from multiple queries. Only a result where Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsQuery.CastResult.\_hit is true is drawn. |
| [DrawShapeProxy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawShapeProxy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawShapeProxy.html") | Draw a ShapeProxy. |
| [DrawTransformAxis](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawTransformAxis.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawTransformAxis.html") | Draw a Transform axis. |
| [Explode](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Explode.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Explode.html") | Apply a radial explosion applying impulses away from the position to all bodies found within in the radius. |
| [GetBodies](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodies.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodies.html") | Get all the active PhysicsBody in the specified world. |
| [GetBodyUpdateCallbackTargets](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodyUpdateCallbackTargets.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodyUpdateCallbackTargets.html") | Get all current PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents where either of the PhysicsBody involved are valid (see PhysicsBody.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsBody.callbackTarget). |
| [GetBodyUpdateOwnerUserData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodyUpdateOwnerUserData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodyUpdateOwnerUserData.html") | Get all PhysicsBody.ownerUserData assigned to each PhysicsBody returned with PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents. The Native Array returned will be of the same length and be ordered the same as the BodyUpdateEvent returned with PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents. Any PhysicsBody that are not valid will return a default PhysicsUserData. |
| [GetBodyUpdateUserData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodyUpdateUserData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetBodyUpdateUserData.html") | Get all PhysicsBody.userData assigned to each PhysicsBody returned with PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents. The Native Array returned will be of the same length and be ordered the same as the BodyUpdateEvent returned with PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents. Any PhysicsBody that are not valid will return a default PhysicsUserData. |
| [GetContactCallbackTargets](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetContactCallbackTargets.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetContactCallbackTargets.html") | Get all current PhysicsWorld.contactBeginEvents and PhysicsWorld.contactEndEvents where either of the PhysicsShape involved are valid (see PhysicsShape.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsShape.callbackTarget). |
| [GetJoints](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetJoints.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetJoints.html") | Get all the active PhysicsJoint in the specified world. |
| [GetJointThresholdCallbackTargets](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetJointThresholdCallbackTargets.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetJointThresholdCallbackTargets.html") | Get all current PhysicsWorld.jointThresholdEvents where either of the PhysicsJoint involved are valid (see PhysicsJoint.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsJoint.callbackTarget). |
| [GetOwner](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetOwner.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetOwner.html") | Get the owner object associated with this world as specified using PhysicsWorld.SetOwner. |
| [GetTransformWriteTweens](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetTransformWriteTweens.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetTransformWriteTweens.html") | Gets all the existing Transform Write Tweens that are handled per-frame. If the PhysicsWorld.transformTweenMode is PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Sequential then the tweens are sorted into ascending transform depth allowing writing to the Transform hierarchy by simply iterating the tweens . If the PhysicsWorld.transformTweenMode is PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Sequential then the tweens are unsorted as a Jobs.TransformAccessArray is used to write them. See TransformWriteTween and TransformWriteMode. The returned Collections.NativeArray\_1 aliases the per-frame internal buffer owned by the world; it does not own its memory (so disposing it does nothing). The contents are only valid until the next simulation step runs, after which the buffer may be reused or destroyed. If a longer-lived copy is required, copy the contents into a caller-owned Collections.NativeArray\_1. |
| [GetTriggerCallbackTargets](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetTriggerCallbackTargets.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetTriggerCallbackTargets.html") | Get all current PhysicsWorld.triggerBeginEvents and PhysicsWorld.triggerEndEvents where either of the PhysicsShape involved are valid (see PhysicsShape.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsShape.callbackTarget). |
| [OverlapAABB](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapAABB.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapAABB.html") | Returns all shapes that potentially overlap the provided AABB. The overlap is between AABB of shapes in the world therefore it may not result in an exact overlap of the shape itself. See PhysicsAABB, QueryFilter, WorldOverlapResult and Collections.Allocator. |
| [OverlapGeometry](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapGeometry.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapGeometry.html") | Returns all shapes that overlap the provided Circle geometry. A circle with a radius of zero is equivalent to PhysicsWorld.OverlapPoint. See CircleGeometry, QueryFilter, WorldOverlapResult and Collections.Allocator |
| [OverlapPoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapPoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapPoint.html") | Returns all shapes that overlap the provided point. This first converts the shape to a ShapeProxy and uses PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapShapeProxy. See QueryFilter, WorldOverlapResult and Collections.Allocator. |
| [OverlapShape](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapShape.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapShape.html") | Returns all shapes that overlap the provided shape. The selected shape is excluded from any results and must be in this world otherwise a warning will be produced. |
| [OverlapShapeProxy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapShapeProxy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.OverlapShapeProxy.html") | Returns all shapes that overlap the shape proxy. See QueryFilter. WorldOverlapResult and Collections.Allocator. |
| [Reset](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Reset.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Reset.html") | Reset the world to a canonical state so that it will reproduce identical results each time. The world must be empty for this to be called otherwise a warning is produced. |
| [SendAllCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendAllCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendAllCallbacks.html") | Send all callbacks to targets: PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacksPhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacksPhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacksPhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks |
| [SendBodyUpdateCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacks.html") | Send all current PhysicsWorld.bodyUpdateEvents where the PhysicsBody involved are valid (see PhysicsBody.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsBody.callbackTarget). Only callback targets that implement IBodyUpdateCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if PhysicsWorld.autoBodyUpdateCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread. |
| [SendContactCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacks.html") | Send all current PhysicsWorld.contactBeginEvents and PhysicsWorld.contactEndEvents where either of the PhysicsShape involved are valid (see PhysicsShape.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsShape.callbackTarget). These events will only be created if both of the shape pairs has PhysicsShape.contactEvents set to true. Only callback targets that implement IContactCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if PhysicsWorld.autoContactCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread. |
| [SendJointThresholdCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks.html") | Send all current PhysicsWorld.jointThresholdEvents where the PhysicsJoint involved are valid (see PhysicsJoint.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsJoint.callbackTarget). These events will only be created if the joint exceeds its PhysicsJoint.forceThreshold or PhysicsJoint.torqueThreshold. Only callback targets that implement IJointThresholdCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if PhysicsWorld.autoJointThresholdCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread. |
| [SendTriggerCallbacks](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacks.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacks.html") | Send all current PhysicsWorld.triggerBeginEvents and PhysicsWorld.triggerEndEvents where either of the PhysicsShape involved are valid (see PhysicsShape.isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see PhysicsShape.callbackTarget). These events will only be created if one of the shape pairs has PhysicsShape.triggerEvents set to true. Only callback targets that implement ITriggerCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if PhysicsWorld.autoTriggerCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread. |
| [SetElementDepth3D](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetElementDepth3D.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetElementDepth3D.html") | Set the element depth using the specified 3D position. The relevant axis will be extracted using the current PhysicsWorld.transformPlane. If PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.Custom is used, the element depth is always set to zero. For more details, see PhysicsWorld.elementDepth. |
| [SetOwnerUserData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwnerUserData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwnerUserData.html") | Set PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only. |
| [Simulate](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Simulate.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Simulate.html") | Simulate the world. If is zero then only contact and trigger events will be updated and no velocity or position integration or constraint updates will occur. |
| [TestOverlapAABB](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapAABB.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapAABB.html") | Tests if the provided AABB potentially overlaps any shapes. The overlap is between AABB of shapes in the world therefore it may not result in an exact overlap of any shape itself. See PhysicsAABB and QueryFilter. |
| [TestOverlapGeometry](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapGeometry.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapGeometry.html") | Tests if the provided Circle geometry overlaps any shapes. A circle with a radius of zero is equivalent to PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapPoint. See CircleGeometry and QueryFilter. |
| [TestOverlapPoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapPoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapPoint.html") | Tests if the provided point overlaps any shapes. See QueryFilter. |
| [TestOverlapShape](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapShape.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapShape.html") | Tests if the provided shape overlaps any shapes. The selected shape is excluded from any results and must be in this world otherwise a warning will be produced. |
| [TestOverlapShapeProxy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapShapeProxy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TestOverlapShapeProxy.html") | Test if the provided shape proxy overlaps any shapes. |

### Static Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [CheckTransformChanges](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CheckTransformChanges.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CheckTransformChanges.html") | Checks for any transform changes. Anything using PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange will immediately be notified of any changes. This should be used sparingly otherwise it may impact performance. The preference should be not using this but instead control transform changes to be monitored with PhysicsWorld.transformChangeMode. |
| [Create](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Create.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Create.html") | Create a PhysicsWorld using the PhysicsWorldDefinition.defaultDefinition. |
| [CreateOwnerKey](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateOwnerKey.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateOwnerKey.html") | Create an owner key. |
| [DestroyBodyBatch](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DestroyBodyBatch.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DestroyBodyBatch.html") | Destroy a batch of bodies. Any invalid bodies will be ignored. Owned bodies will produce a warning and will not be destroyed (See PhysicsBody.SetOwner). |
| [DestroyJointBatch](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DestroyJointBatch.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DestroyJointBatch.html") | Destroy a batch of joints. Any invalid joints will be ignored. Owned joints will produce a warning and will not be destroyed (PhysicsJoint.SetOwner). |
| [DestroyShapeBatch](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DestroyShapeBatch.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DestroyShapeBatch.html") | Destroy a batch of shapes, destroying all Contact the shapes are involved in. Any invalid shapes will be ignored including chain segment shapes created via a PhysicsChain (the chain must be destroyed)." Owned shapes will produce a warning and will not be destroyed (PhysicsShape.SetOwner). See MassConfiguration. |
| [GetWorlds](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetWorlds.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.GetWorlds.html") | Get all the active PhysicsWorld. This includes the PhysicsWorld.defaultWorld so will always contain at least a single world. |
| [RegisterTransformChange](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange.html") | Register a transform watcher to call the specified callback when a transform changes. See TransformChangeEvent for the types of transform changes that are watched for. You MUST unregister this when no longer needed with PhysicsWorld.UnregisterTransformChange otherwise you will receive warnings. |
| [SetOwner](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwner.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwner.html") | Set the owner object using the specified owner key. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. This call does not bind the lifetime of the specified owner object, it is simply a reference. Whilst it is valid to not specify an owner object (NULL), it is recommended for debugging purposes. |
| [SetTransform](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetTransform.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetTransform.html") | Set the Transform position without causing a TransformChangeEvent to be generated by default. See PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange. |
| [SetTransformAccess](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetTransformAccess.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetTransformAccess.html") | Set the Jobs.TransformAccess position without causing a TransformChangeEvent to be generated. See PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange. |
| [UnregisterTransformChange](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.UnregisterTransformChange.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.UnregisterTransformChange.html") | Unregister a transform watched to stop calling the specified callback when a transform changes. See TransformChangeEvent for the types of transform changes that are watched for. |

## Declaration

public int GetPositions(out [NativeSlice<Vector3>](Unity.Collections.NativeSlice_1.html "Unity.Collections.NativeSlice_1.html") positions);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| positions | The array of positions to retrieve. |

### Returns

**int**
How many positions were actually stored in the output array.

### Description

Get the positions of all vertices in the trail.

This method is preferred to [GetPosition](TrailRenderer.GetPosition.html "TrailRenderer.GetPosition.html") when retrieving all positions, as it is more efficient to get all positions using a single command than to get each position individually.  
  
Additional resources: [positionCount](TrailRenderer-positionCount.html "TrailRenderer-positionCount.html") property.  
  
Additional resources: [GetPosition](TrailRenderer.GetPosition.html "TrailRenderer.GetPosition.html") function.

### Description

Provides access to a display or screen for rendering operations.

Unity supports multi-display rendering on the following platforms:

* Desktop platforms (Windows, macOS, and Linux)
* Android (OpenGL ES and Vulkan)
* iOS
* Embedded Linux
* QNX

Some features in the `Display` class only work on some of the supported platforms. For more information about platform compatibility, refer to the individual properties and methods.  
  
Use the `Display` class to operate on the displays and [Camera.targetDisplay](Camera-targetDisplay.html "Camera-targetDisplay.html") to set up cameras for rendering to individual displays.  
  
Additional resources: [Camera.targetDisplay](Camera-targetDisplay.html "Camera-targetDisplay.html"), [Canvas.targetDisplay](Canvas-targetDisplay.html "Canvas-targetDisplay.html").

```
using UnityEngine;  
  
public class Example : MonoBehaviour
{
    Camera extCam;
    Camera cam;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        // GUI is rendered with last camera.
        // As we want it to end up in the main screen, make sure main camera is the last one drawn.
        extCam.depth = cam.depth - 1;  
  
        cam.SetTargetBuffers(Display.main.colorBuffer, Display.main.depthBuffer);
        extCam.enabled = false;
    }  
  
    void Update()
    {
        if (Display.displays.Length > 1 && !extCam.enabled)
        {
            Display.displays[1].SetRenderingResolution(256, 256);
            extCam.SetTargetBuffers(Display.displays[1].colorBuffer, Display.displays[1].depthBuffer);
        }
        extCam.enabled = Display.displays.Length > 1;
    }
}
```

| [main](Display-main.html "Display-main.html") | Main Display. |

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [active](Display-active.html "Display-active.html") | Gets the state of the display and returns true if the display is active and false if otherwise. |
| [colorBuffer](Display-colorBuffer.html "Display-colorBuffer.html") | Color RenderBuffer. |
| [depthBuffer](Display-depthBuffer.html "Display-depthBuffer.html") | Depth RenderBuffer. |
| [renderingHeight](Display-renderingHeight.html "Display-renderingHeight.html") | Vertical resolution that the display is rendering at. |
| [renderingWidth](Display-renderingWidth.html "Display-renderingWidth.html") | Horizontal resolution that the display is rendering at in the viewport. |
| [requiresBlitToBackbuffer](Display-requiresBlitToBackbuffer.html "Display-requiresBlitToBackbuffer.html") | True when the back buffer requires an intermediate texture to render. |
| [requiresSrgbBlitToBackbuffer](Display-requiresSrgbBlitToBackbuffer.html "Display-requiresSrgbBlitToBackbuffer.html") | True when doing a blit to the back buffer requires manual color space conversion. |
| [systemHeight](Display-systemHeight.html "Display-systemHeight.html") | Vertical native display resolution. |
| [systemWidth](Display-systemWidth.html "Display-systemWidth.html") | Horizontal native display resolution. |

| [SetRenderingResolution](Display.SetRenderingResolution.html "Display.SetRenderingResolution.html") | Sets rendering resolution for the display. |

public long CurrentValue;

### Description

Gets current value of the Profiler metric.

Use to obtain immediate profiler counter value or marker timing.
If the current value is the only data you are interested in, there is no need to start ProfilerRecorder or allocate sample storage. In this case use 0 as a capacity parameter when creating ProfilerRecorder.

```
using UnityEngine;
using Unity.Profiling;  
  
public class Example
{
    public static void LogCurrentSystemMemoryUsage()
    {
        var systemMemoryRecorder = new ProfilerRecorder(ProfilerCategory.Memory, "System Used Memory", 0);
        Debug.Log("System Used Memory (bytes): " + systemMemoryRecorder.CurrentValue);
    }
}
```

Use *CurrentValue* to retrieve timings of a code tagged with [ProfilerMarker.Auto](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Auto.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Auto.html").

```
using UnityEngine;
using Unity.Profiling;  
  
public class Example
{
    static readonly ProfilerMarker k_MyMarker = new ProfilerMarker(ProfilerCategory.Scripts, "MyMarker");  
  
    public static void TimeSynchronousMethodWithMarkers()
    {
        using (var recorder = ProfilerRecorder.StartNew(ProfilerCategory.Scripts, "MyMarker"))
        {
            using (k_MyMarker.Auto())
            {
                // ...
            }  
  
            Debug.Log("MyMarker total time, ns:  " + recorder.CurrentValue);
        }
    }
}
```

**Note:**
  
[Stop](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerRecorder.Stop.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerRecorder.Stop.html") resets *CurrentValue* to zero.

public bool generateLightingData;

### Description

Configures a line to generate Normals and Tangents. With this data, Scene lighting can affect the line via Normal Maps and the Unity Standard Shader, or your own custom-built Shaders.

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
[RequireComponent(typeof(LineRenderer))]
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    private LineRenderer lr;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        lr = GetComponent<LineRenderer>();
        lr.material = new Material(Shader.Find("Standard"));
        lr.generateLightingData = true;  
  
        // Set some positions
        Vector3[] positions = new Vector3[3];
        positions[0] = new Vector3(-2.0f, -2.0f, 0.0f);
        positions[1] = new Vector3(0.0f, 2.0f, 0.0f);
        positions[2] = new Vector3(2.0f, -2.0f, 0.0f);
        lr.positionCount = positions.Length;
        lr.SetPositions(positions);
    }
}
```

## Declaration

public Color32[] GetPixels32(Color32[] colors = null);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| colors | An optional array to write the pixel data to. |

### Returns

**Color32[]**
An array that contains the pixel colors.

### Description

Gets the pixel color data for a mipmap level as [Color32](Color32.html "Color32.html") structs.

This method gets pixel data from the texture in CPU memory. [Texture.isReadable](Texture-isReadable.html "Texture-isReadable.html") must be `true`.  
  
The array contains the pixels row by row, starting at the bottom left of the texture. The size of the array is the width × height of the texture.   
  
Each pixel is a [Color32](Color32.html "Color32.html") struct.  
  
A single call to `GetPixels32` is usually faster than multiple calls to [GetPixel](WebCamTexture.GetPixel.html "WebCamTexture.GetPixel.html"), especially for large textures.  
  
If `GetPixels32` fails, Unity throws an exception. `GetPixels32` might fail if the array contains too much data.  
  
You can optionally pass in an array of [Color32](Color32.html "Color32.html") structs to avoid allocating new memory each frame. This can improve performance if you are continuously reading data from the camera. The array must be initialized to the dimensions `width * height` of the texture. If you don't pass an array, Unity will allocate one and return it.

```
using UnityEngine;  
  
public class Example : MonoBehaviour
{
    WebCamTexture webcamTexture;
    Color32[] data;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        // Start web cam feed
        webcamTexture = new WebCamTexture();
        webcamTexture.Play();
        data = new Color32[webcamTexture.width * webcamTexture.height];
    }  
  
    void Update()
    {
        webcamTexture.GetPixels32(data);
        // Do processing of data here.
    }
}
```

### Description

Editor-only function that Unity calls when the script is loaded or a value changes in the Inspector.

`OnValidate` is usually used to perform an action after a value changes in the Inspector. For example, making sure that data stays within a certain range.  
  
The following operations aren't supported and can cause errors in your application when performed from `OnValidate`:

* Modifying values on another script.
* Calling [ScriptableSingleton.Save](ScriptableSingleton_1.Save.html "ScriptableSingleton_1.Save.html").
* Camera rendering operations. A safe alternative is to add a listener to [EditorApplication.update](EditorApplication-update.html "EditorApplication-update.html") and perform the rendering during the next Editor Update call.

## Declaration

public static bool IsPlatformIncluded(string buildTargetGroupName,
int index);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| buildTargetGroupName | The platform name. |
| index | The index of the Quality Level, must be positive and lower than the count of Quality Levels. |

### Returns

**bool**
If the platform is included.

### Description

[Editor Only] Returns if the given platform is included by the Quality Level.

```
    public bool IsPlatformIcluded(BuildTarget platform, int index)
    {
        var activeBuildTargetGroup = BuildPipeline.GetBuildTargetGroup(platform);
        var namedBuildTarget = NamedBuildTarget.FromBuildTargetGroup(activeBuildTargetGroup);
        return QualitySettings.IsPlatformIncluded(namedBuildTarget.TargetName, index);
    }
```

### Description

Generate a depth + normals texture.

Will generate a screen-space depth and view space normals texture as seen from this camera.
Texture will be in [RenderTextureFormat.ARGB32](RenderTextureFormat.ARGB32.html "RenderTextureFormat.ARGB32.html") format and will be set as `_CameraDepthNormalsTexture`

public static bool forceAssetUnloadAndGCOnSceneLoad;

### Description

Submit suggestion

Cancel

**Obsolete** 
Use SubsystemWithProvider instead.

### Description

A Subsystem is initialized from a [SubsystemDescriptorWithProvider](SubsystemsImplementation.SubsystemDescriptorWithProvider.html "SubsystemsImplementation.SubsystemDescriptorWithProvider.html") for a given Subsystem (Example, Input, Display, etc.) and provides an interface to interact with that given Subsystem until it is Destroyed. After a Subsystem is created it can be Started or Stopped to turn on and off functionality (and improve performance). The base type for subsystems only exposes this functionality; this class is designed to be a base class for derived classes that expose more functionality specific to a given Subsystem.  
  
 Note: initializing a second Subsystem from the same SubsystemDescriptor will return a reference to the existing Subsystem as only one Subsystem is currently allowed for a single Subsystem provider.  
  
This subsystem base-class is deprecated. If you are creating a new subsystem type, derive from [SubsystemWithProvider](SubsystemsImplementation.SubsystemWithProvider.html "SubsystemsImplementation.SubsystemWithProvider.html") instead.

public bool applyToCollection;

### Description

Makes attribute affect collections instead of their items.

When you apply a `PropertyAttribute` to a collection, by default Unity applies it to each element of the collection. When `applyToCollection` is `true`, the attribute is applied to the collection itself instead.  
  
You can use this in scenarios where the attribute functionality needs to apply to the collection as a whole rather than per element. Some typical scenarios include:

* A reorderable list header or collection-level label. For example, when creating a drawer that adds a summary line stating the total number of items in the list, or a custom add or remove toolbar.
* An attribute that makes a list non-reorderable, or locks its size.
* Validation across the collection. For example, an attribute that checks that a list contains unique entries or that it has at least three items.

```
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEditor.UIElements;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.UIElements;  
  
public class Collection : MonoBehaviour
{
    public int before;
    [GreenCollectionDrawer] public int[] collection;
    public int after;
}  
  
public class GreenCollectionDrawerAttribute : PropertyAttribute
{
    public GreenCollectionDrawerAttribute() : base(true) { }
}  
  
[CustomPropertyDrawer(typeof(GreenCollectionDrawerAttribute))]
public class GreenCollectionDrawer : PropertyDrawer
{
    public override VisualElement CreatePropertyGUI(SerializedProperty property)
    {
        return new PropertyField(property)
        {
            style =
            {
                backgroundColor = Color.green
            }
        };
    }
}
```

### Description

Render stereo to the left and right halves of a single, double-width render target.

In side-by-side single-pass stereo rendering, the rendering pipeline traverses the scene graph only once while issuing two draw calls for each render node. Each eye is rendered to one side of the render target. The main render target must be a twice as wide as a single-eye target. Scene culling and shadow map rendering is shared between both eyes. Side-by-side rendering is significantly faster than multi-pass rendering for VR, but is a little slower than instancing or multiview modes.

### Description

Use the DragLeaveEvent class to manage events sent when dragging leaves an element or one of its descendants. The DragLeaveEvent does not trickle down and does not bubble up.

### Constructors

| Constructor | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [DragLeaveEvent](UIElements.DragLeaveEvent-ctor.html "UIElements.DragLeaveEvent-ctor.html") | Constructor. Avoid renewing events. Instead, use GetPooled() to get an event from a pool of reusable events. |

### Protected Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Init](UIElements.DragLeaveEvent.Init.html "UIElements.DragLeaveEvent.Init.html") | Resets the event members to their initial values. |

### Inherited Members

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [bubbles](UIElements.EventBase-bubbles.html "UIElements.EventBase-bubbles.html") | Returns whether this event type bubbles up in the event propagation path during the BubbleUp phase. |
| [dispatch](UIElements.EventBase-dispatch.html "UIElements.EventBase-dispatch.html") | Indicates whether the event is being dispatched to a visual element. An event cannot be redispatched while it being dispatched. If you need to recursively dispatch an event, it is recommended that you use a copy of the event. |
| [ignoreDisabledElements](UIElements.EventBase-ignoreDisabledElements.html "UIElements.EventBase-ignoreDisabledElements.html") | If this property is true, callbacks for this event are not invoked when the current target is disabled, unless those callbacks are registered using the CallbackOptions.IncludeDisabled option. |
| [imguiEvent](UIElements.EventBase-imguiEvent.html "UIElements.EventBase-imguiEvent.html") | The IMGUIEvent at the source of this event. The source can be null since not all events are generated by IMGUI. |
| [isImmediatePropagationStopped](UIElements.EventBase-isImmediatePropagationStopped.html "UIElements.EventBase-isImmediatePropagationStopped.html") | Indicates whether EventBase.StopImmediatePropagation was called for this event. |
| [isPropagationStopped](UIElements.EventBase-isPropagationStopped.html "UIElements.EventBase-isPropagationStopped.html") | Returns true if EventBase.StopPropagation or EventBase.StopImmediatePropagation was called for this event. |
| [originalMousePosition](UIElements.EventBase-originalMousePosition.html "UIElements.EventBase-originalMousePosition.html") | The original mouse position of the IMGUI event, before it is transformed to the current target local coordinates. |
| [pooled](UIElements.EventBase-pooled.html "UIElements.EventBase-pooled.html") | Whether the event is allocated from a pool of events. |
| [propagationPhase](UIElements.EventBase-propagationPhase.html "UIElements.EventBase-propagationPhase.html") | The current propagation phase for this event. |
| [target](UIElements.EventBase-target.html "UIElements.EventBase-target.html") | The target visual element that received this event. Unlike currentTarget, this target does not change when the event is sent to other elements along the propagation path. |
| [timestamp](UIElements.EventBase-timestamp.html "UIElements.EventBase-timestamp.html") | The time when the event was dispatched, in milliseconds. |
| [tricklesDown](UIElements.EventBase-tricklesDown.html "UIElements.EventBase-tricklesDown.html") | Returns whether this event is sent down the event propagation path during the TrickleDown phase. |
| [eventTypeId](UIElements.EventBase_1-eventTypeId.html "UIElements.EventBase_1-eventTypeId.html") | See EventBase.eventTypeId. |
| [actionKey](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-actionKey.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-actionKey.html") | Returns true if the platform-specific action key is pressed. |
| [altKey](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-altKey.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-altKey.html") | Returns true if the Alt key is pressed. |
| [button](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-button.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-button.html") | A value that indicates which mouse button was pressed or released (if any) to cause this event: 0 is the left button, 1 is the right button, 2 is the middle button. A negative value indicates that no mouse button changed state during this event. |
| [clickCount](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-clickCount.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-clickCount.html") | The number of times a button is pressed consecutively. |
| [commandKey](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-commandKey.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-commandKey.html") | Returns true if the Windows/Cmd key is pressed. |
| [ctrlKey](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-ctrlKey.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-ctrlKey.html") | Returns true if the Ctrl key is pressed. |
| [currentTarget](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-currentTarget.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-currentTarget.html") | The current target of the event. The current target is the element in the propagation path for which event handlers are currently being executed. |
| [localMousePosition](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-localMousePosition.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-localMousePosition.html") | The mouse position in the current target coordinate system. |
| [modifiers](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-modifiers.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-modifiers.html") | Flags that hold pressed modifier keys (Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Windows/Cmd). |
| [mouseDelta](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-mouseDelta.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-mouseDelta.html") | Gets the difference between the mouse's position during the previous mouse event and its position during the current mouse event. |
| [mousePosition](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-mousePosition.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-mousePosition.html") | The mouse position in the panel coordinate system. |
| [pressedButtons](UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-pressedButtons.html "UIElements.MouseEventBase_1-pressedButtons.html") | A bitmask that describes the currently pressed buttons. |

public static int defaultScreenHeight;

### Description

Default vertical dimension of stand-alone player window.

![](../StaticFiles/ScriptRefImages/PlayerSettingsCustomSettings.png)
  
*Custom player settings.*

```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEditor;  
  

// Simple Script that saves and loads custom
// Stand-alone/Web player screen settings among
// Unity Projects  
  
class CustomSettings : EditorWindow
{  
  
    string compName = "";
    string prodName = "";
    int screenWidth = 640;
    int screenHeight = 480;
    int webScreenWidth = 640;
    int webScreenHeight = 480;
    bool fullScreen = false;  
  
    [MenuItem("Examples/Custom Settings")]
        static void Init()
    {
        var window = GetWindow<CustomSettings>();
        window.Show();
    }  
  
    void OnGUI()
    {
        compName = EditorGUILayout.TextField("Company Name:", compName);
        prodName = EditorGUILayout.TextField("Product Name:", prodName);
        EditorGUILayout.BeginHorizontal();
        screenWidth = EditorGUILayout.IntField("Width:", screenWidth);
        screenHeight = EditorGUILayout.IntField("Web Height:", screenHeight);
        EditorGUILayout.EndHorizontal();
        EditorGUILayout.Space();
        EditorGUILayout.BeginHorizontal();
        webScreenWidth = EditorGUILayout.IntField("Web Width:", webScreenWidth);
        webScreenHeight = EditorGUILayout.IntField("Web Height:", webScreenHeight);
        EditorGUILayout.EndHorizontal();
        fullScreen = EditorGUILayout.Toggle("Full Screen:", fullScreen);
        EditorGUILayout.BeginHorizontal();
        if (GUILayout.Button("Save Values"))
            SaveSettings();
        if (GUILayout.Button("Load Values"))
            LoadSettings();
        EditorGUILayout.EndHorizontal();
    }  
  
    void SaveSettings()
    {
        PlayerSettings.companyName = compName;
        PlayerSettings.productName = prodName;
        PlayerSettings.defaultScreenWidth = screenWidth;
        PlayerSettings.defaultScreenHeight = screenHeight;
        PlayerSettings.defaultWebScreenWidth = webScreenWidth;
        PlayerSettings.defaultWebScreenHeight = webScreenHeight;
        PlayerSettings.defaultIsFullScreen = fullScreen;  
  
        EditorPrefs.SetString("CompName", compName);
        EditorPrefs.SetString("ProdName", prodName);
        EditorPrefs.SetInt("ScreenWidth", screenWidth);
        EditorPrefs.SetInt("ScreenHeight", screenHeight);
        EditorPrefs.SetInt("WebScreenWidth", webScreenWidth);
        EditorPrefs.SetInt("WebScreenHeight", webScreenHeight);
    }
    void LoadSettings()
    {
        compName = EditorPrefs.GetString("CompName", "");
        prodName = EditorPrefs.GetString("ProdName", "");
        screenWidth = EditorPrefs.GetInt("ScreenWidth", 640);
        screenHeight = EditorPrefs.GetInt("ScreenHeight", 480);
        webScreenWidth = EditorPrefs.GetInt("WebScreenWidth", 640);
        webScreenHeight = EditorPrefs.GetInt("WebScreenHeight", 480);
    }
}
```

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-ParticleSystem.html "Go to ParticleSystem Component in the Manual")

public bool enabled;

### Description

Specifies whether the VelocityOverLifetimeModule is enabled or disabled.

Additional resources: [ParticleSystem.velocityOverLifetime](ParticleSystem-velocityOverLifetime.html "ParticleSystem-velocityOverLifetime.html").

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
[RequireComponent(typeof(ParticleSystem))]
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    private ParticleSystem ps;
    public float hSliderValueX = 1.0f;
    public float hSliderValueY = 1.0f;
    public float hSliderValueZ = 1.0f;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        ps = GetComponent<ParticleSystem>();  
  
        var velocityOverLifetime = ps.velocityOverLifetime;
        velocityOverLifetime.enabled = true;
        velocityOverLifetime.space = ParticleSystemSimulationSpace.World;  
  
        AnimationCurve curve = new AnimationCurve();
        curve.AddKey(0.0f, 0.0f);
        curve.AddKey(1.0f, 1.0f);  
  
        ParticleSystem.MinMaxCurve minMaxCurve = new ParticleSystem.MinMaxCurve(1.0f, curve);  
  
        velocityOverLifetime.x = minMaxCurve;
        velocityOverLifetime.y = minMaxCurve;
        velocityOverLifetime.z = minMaxCurve;  
  
        var psr = GetComponent<ParticleSystemRenderer>();
        psr.material = new Material(Shader.Find("Sprites/Default"));    // this material renders a square billboard, making it easier to see the size
    }  
  
    void Update()
    {
        var velocityOverLifetime = ps.velocityOverLifetime;
        velocityOverLifetime.xMultiplier = hSliderValueX;
        velocityOverLifetime.yMultiplier = hSliderValueY;
        velocityOverLifetime.zMultiplier = hSliderValueZ;
    }  
  
    void OnGUI()
    {
        GUI.Label(new Rect(25, 40, 100, 30), "X");
        GUI.Label(new Rect(25, 80, 100, 30), "Y");
        GUI.Label(new Rect(25, 120, 100, 30), "Z");  
  
        hSliderValueX = GUI.HorizontalSlider(new Rect(55, 45, 100, 30), hSliderValueX, -50.0f, 50.0f);
        hSliderValueY = GUI.HorizontalSlider(new Rect(55, 85, 100, 30), hSliderValueY, -50.0f, 50.0f);
        hSliderValueZ = GUI.HorizontalSlider(new Rect(55, 125, 100, 30), hSliderValueZ, -50.0f, 50.0f);
    }
}
```
